issue_context.title: BUG: AttributeError: 'BooleanArray' object has no attribute 'sum' while infer types
issue_context.body:
Line 694 in the pandas/io/parsers/base_parser.py file, 
```
        if issubclass(values.dtype.type, (np.number, np.bool_)):
            # error: Argument 2 to "isin" has incompatible type "List[Any]"; expected
            # "Union[Union[ExtensionArray, ndarray], Index, Series]"
            mask = algorithms.isin(values, list(na_values))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            na_count =mask.sum()
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^THIS
            if na_count > 0:
                if is_integer_dtype(values):
                    values = values.astype(np.float64)
                np.putmask(values, mask, np.nan)
            return values, na_count
```

Caused an "AttributeError: 'BooleanArray' object has no attribute 'sum'" following some global ananconda update. Changed the line to 
`            na_count =mask.astype('uint8').sum()`

fixed the error in my case.

Edit by rhshadrach:

Minimal example

```
from io import StringIO

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv(
     StringIO("0,1"),
     names=['a', 'b'],
     index_col=['a'],
     dtype={'a': 'UInt8'},
)
```

review_comments: why is the check_index_type=False? can we not construct the appropriate expected?

It's actually the results not the expected. Two parser are currently under test, the C parser returns a index column of dtype 'object' and the Python parser returns a index column of dtype 'int64'. Both result are inferred, and both make sense in this specific example. Unifying the behavior of the parsers is desirable but beyond the scope of the current bug fix.
